lines.text: The ozone hole is actually healing.
In sixty seconds, you'll know the truth.
High in the sky, ozone blocks harmful ultraviolet rays.
In the 1980s, scientists found a hole over Antarctica.
Keep watching for fact three. It's the big one.
Fact one. Chemicals called CFCs, from fridges and sprays, were destroying it.
Fact two. In 1987, countries signed the Montreal Protocol to phase them out.
And the big one. Experts expect most of the world to recover by around 2040.
And the Antarctic hole during the twenty-sixties.
Verdict. 'It can't be fixed' is false.
Global action worked, and recovery is on track.
Did you know the ozone hole was healing? Yes or no. Comment below, and follow Paravion X for more.

meta.summary: CFCs from fridges and sprays damaged the ozone layer. The 1987 Montreal Protocol phased them out. The 2026 UNEP/WMO Scientific Assessment expects recovery around 2040 for most of the world and during the 2060s over Antarctica. It no longer gives a specific Arctic return year.
